summary:
Backend and platform work on Vend's messaging platform — four Nordic marketplaces (finn.no, blocket.se, tori.fi, dba.dk), one codebase after a near-zero-downtime consolidation, ~30 microservices on Kubernetes, 120M+ requests/day on the largest leg. The part I keep returning to is the cross-brand seam — where one brand's change becomes four brands' problem, the boundary no single team owns by default. Occasional frontend forays when a change needs to land end-to-end.

Currently building Vend Assistant, an LLM-mediated buyer/seller surface inside the messaging thread — POC through to production shape, adjacent to the team's substrate, not around it.
Open banking under PSD2. Data-sharing APIs for Skatteetaten and Politi. Small team, end-to-end ownership, the kind of code review where the bar is set by the person asking the sharpest question.

Cards platform — global, millions of transactions a day. Led a team to ship a new microservice in two months. Ran a cloud infrastructure pilot on GCP + Pub/Sub, shelved by COVID budget cuts. Agile lead through the org's Atlassian migration.
Identity & access management (STIM), internal React + Spring app, GDPR document-redactor POC on Google Cloud OCR.

company: Tata Consultancy Services - Posten Norge / Bring
summary: Distributed Agile team building the logistics web platform for Posten Norge / Bring — 20+ Java web applications, 15–20 deploys a day, an in-house DevOps + monitoring framework we built because nothing off-the-shelf fit. A rotational posting: a few years in Oslo, the rest back in India between Delhi and Mumbai. Test-code volume exceeded production-code volume, deliberately. Grew into team-lead responsibility. The high-cadence, delete-first engineering discipline I run on today started here.
Trained cohorts of 30–35 new joiners on core Java and J2EE. Teacher before I was an engineer.

Technical lead on a credit-rating platform for a European investment bank — functional analysis, technical design, code review, and deploys through SIT/UAT. Ran the sprint ceremonies alongside the build.

Two years for the University of the Witwatersrand — a student admissions and progression rules engine, then a Peoplesoft Campus Solutions enrolments rollout. Grew from building the engine to owning the functional analysis on the platform side.

items.name: Peoplesoft Campus Solutions — Enrolments
items.blurb: Enrolments module for Campus Solutions, end-to-end — requirements gathering through SIT/UAT.

items.name: Admissions & Progression Rules Engine
items.blurb: Designed and shipped a rules engine for student admissions and progression — including a plain-English abstraction layer so non-engineers could read and reason about the rules.

summary: First job. Three years of Java/J2EE financial platforms for two clients — TATA Capital and AXIS Bank. Mutual funds, fixed deposits, vendor reference data, a trading-portal CMS — the origin of the financial-platform work. Started as a developer, grew into technical lead on the back-office and reconciliation systems.

items.name: AXIS Direct
items.blurb: Online trading portal for AXIS Bank customers on Weblogic Portal, integrated with eibs front and back office. Built the CMS — screens, application forms, PDFs, video tutorials — and the interface engine pulling live market data (Geodesic, Capital Markets) and research feeds (Thomson Reuters, CRISIL).

items.name: TCL VRDMS — Vendor Reference Data Management System
items.blurb: A bridge across TATA Capital's trading and finance systems (eibs, mutual funds, Bancs, SAP-GL) that dedupes and links unique vendors out of a huge messy dataset into one bird's-eye view. Built the file-upload and reconciliation algorithm interfacing six applications.

items.name: Fixed Deposit Trading System
items.blurb: Two apps: an investor UI for placing FD orders and moving funds across banks, and an admin console for plans, rates, roles, registrar instruction/response files, reconciliation, and generating FD forms and cheques.

items.name: Mutual Fund Online Trading & Back Office
items.blurb: India's first online mutual-fund trading platform — the mutual-fund counterpart to eibs, the firm's existing stock-trading platform. Built the user-facing frontend, where investors place orders online or via call centre, and the administration backend that ran it: AMCs, schemes, brokerage rates, batch runs, RTA file loading, transaction reconciliation, brokerage rules, and sub-broker payments.

items.name: MF Lead Distribution System
items.blurb: A fast temporary bridge to capture mutual-fund investment requests from existing eibs investors. Two apps, secured login, wired into the trading product.
